A Greenpoint Private Museum Is No Longer

Faurschou New York, a private art museum in Brooklyn's Greenpoint neighborhood, will no longer host exhibitions as its building is slated for demolition to make way for condos. The institution closed "for renovations" last year, and now its founder, collector Jens Faurschou, officially announced in a statement that the museum will not be reopening. “After forty years, my direction changes,” he wrote. “I will focus on what is essential: my family, private dealing, and working closely with artists, institutions, and collections.”

The space started as Galleri Faurschou in Copenhagen in 1986 and later expanded to Beijing. The New York outpost was opened in 2019, hosting exhibitions including Ai Weiwei's What You See Is What You See , a 2024 show that Hyperallergic 's co-founder and editor-at-large Hrag Vartanian said pushed viewers “to assert our own agency in our interpretations.”
